outlook: Grains finished mostly lower Thursday as traders evened up positions ahead of Friday's USDA WASDE and Crop Production reports. November soybeans fell 10 cents to $12.87½ and December corn slipped 1¾ cents to $5.00¼, with weekly export sales for both near the low end of trade expectations and harvest pressure weighing; analysts expect USDA to trim the corn yield to about 177.7 bu/acre from 178.5 and leave soybean yield unchanged. Wheat was firmer at midday on wheat export sales near the high end of expectations, but faded late: Minneapolis December spring wheat settled about 4 cents lower at $7.06 and December Chicago wheat lost 3¼ cents to $6.83¼. ICE November canola eased about C$3 to C$820.30 as soybean oil weakened, and Minneapolis terminal spring wheat bids held at December futures (zero basis).
